Statistical re-analysis plan: Predicting body fat proportion using anthropometric measures

Mariana Nold

Run Task Bodyfat simplified first.

Load R packages

## [1] 8.381192
rmf <- as.formula(Fat ~ Waist + Height + Weight + Age + Neck + Chest +  
                          Biceps + Hips + Forearm 
                        +  Knee +  Ankle + BMI)

# Fit a Bayesian Gaussian regression model using stan_glm 
ref_fit <- stan_glm(rmf, data = women, family = gaussian())
# Check reference model, MCMC check
summary(ref_fit)
#shinystan::launch_shinystan(ref_fitf)

mcmc_areas(as.matrix(ref_fit)[,2:13])

Investigate quality of the reference model
prior_summary(ref_fit) # https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rstanarm/vignettes/priors.html
## Priors for model 'ref_fit' 
## ------
## Intercept (after predictors centered)
##   Specified prior:
##     ~ normal(location = 22, scale = 2.5)
##   Adjusted prior:
##     ~ normal(location = 22, scale = 15)
## 
## Coefficients
##   Specified prior:
##     ~ normal(location = [0,0,0,...], scale = [2.5,2.5,2.5,...])
##   Adjusted prior:
##     ~ normal(location = [0,0,0,...], scale = [14.53,14.53,14.53,...])
## 
## Auxiliary (sigma)
##   Specified prior:
##     ~ exponential(rate = 1)
##   Adjusted prior:
##     ~ exponential(rate = 0.17)
## ------
## See help('prior_summary.stanreg') for more details
pp_check(ref_fit)

y_rep_rmf <- posterior_predict(ref_fit)
loo_rmf <- loo(ref_fit , save_psis = TRUE, cores = 4)
psis1_rmf <- loo_rmf$psis_object
lw_rmf <- weights(psis1_rmf)
color_scheme_set("red")
#pdf(file.path(PPath, "/LOOPITrmf.pdf"))
ppc_loo_pit_overlay(y = women$Fat,yrep=y_rep_rmf,lw=lw_rmf)
## NOTE: The kernel density estimate assumes continuous observations and is not optimal for discrete observations.

#dev.off()

# Summarize the posterior distributions simple model
summary_rmf_cv <- prediction_summary_cv(model = ref_fit , data = women, k = 3)

# Print the summary simple model
print(summary_rmf_cv)

Use projpred to downsize model even more
set.seed(2341)
vs_cvf <- cv_varsel(ref_fit, method = 'forward', cv_method = 'loo')

save(vs_cvf,file = file.path(PPath,"vs_cvf"))
#load(file = file.path(PPath,"vs_cvf"))


plot(vs_cvf, deltas = TRUE, stats =  c('elpd','rmse'))

Use 5-fold cross validation instead
set.seed(2341)
vs_cvs <- cv_varsel(
  object = ref_fit,         
  cv_method = "kfold",      
  K = 5,                   
  method = "forward",        
  validate_search = TRUE, verbose = FALSE  
)

L1 serach (LOO)

# Generate model path: By varying lambda, a sequence of submodels with an increasing number of (non-zero) coefficients is created. ➤ The order in which coefficients “appear” serves as a ranking of the variables.

set.seed(2341)
vs_cvl <- cv_varsel(ref_fit, method = 'L1', verbose = FALSE)
## Warning in warn_pareto(n07 = sum(pareto_k > 0.7), n05 = sum(0.7 >= pareto_k & :
## In the calculation of the reference model's PSIS-LOO CV weights, 1 (out of 184)
## Pareto k-values are in the interval (0.5, 0.7]. Moment matching (see the loo
## package), mixture importance sampling (see the loo package), and `reloo`-ing
## (see the brms package) are not supported by projpred. If these techniques (run
## outside of projpred, i.e., for the reference model only; note that `reloo`-ing
## may be computationally costly) result in a markedly different reference model
## ELPD estimate than ordinary PSIS-LOO CV does, we recommend to use K-fold CV
## within projpred.
save(vs_cvl,file = file.path(PPath,"vs_cvl"))
#load(file = file.path(PPath,"vs_cvl"))

# Plot the variable selection 

plot(vs_cvl, deltas = TRUE, stats =  c('elpd','rmse'))

#

resultl$summary    # inspect summary
print(resultl$plot)  # view the plot

cumpropl <- cv_proportions(ranking(vs_cvl), cumulate = TRUE) 
rounded_resultl <- get_cumprop_row_rounded(cumpropl, size = 5)
print(rounded_resultl)

# https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/projpred/vignettes/projpred.html#post-selection-inference
proj_ref_fit <- project(vs_cvl, predictor_terms = solterms_final_fivel, ns = 4000)
Show results
color_scheme_set(scheme = "green")
mat <- as.matrix(proj_ref_fit)
beta_std <- mat[, 2:(ncol(mat) - 1)]

# Transform matrix to draws format (optional, for posterior-friendly summaries)
draws1 <- posterior::as_draws_matrix(beta_std)

summarise_draws(draws1, mean, sd, median, ~quantile(.x, probs = c(0.05, 0.95)))

formula_male <- as.formula(Fat ~ Waist  + Hips + BMI + Knee + Biceps)
Model diagnostics (1.3.3)
y_linpred_female <- proj_linpred(proj_ref_fit, solution_terms= solterms_final_fivel, newdata = women)
women2 <- cbind(women, linpred = colMeans(y_linpred_female$pred))
plotLocBias <- ggplot(data.frame(fitted.values = women2$linpred, y = women2$Fat), aes(x=fitted.values, y=y)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth() + geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0)
plotLocBias
## `geom_smooth()` using method = 'loess' and formula = 'y ~ x'

# Compute residuals
prj_predictW <- proj_predict(proj_ref_fit)

qres.m1=createDHARMa(simulatedResponse = t(prj_predictW ), 
                          observedResponse = women2$Fat, 
                          fittedPredictedResponse = apply(prj_predictW , 2, median), integerResponse = F, seed = 123, method = "PIT") 
summary(residuals(qres.m1))
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##  0.0050  0.2669  0.4850  0.4976  0.7325  0.9925
# QQ-Plot 
res <- qnorm(residuals(qres.m1))

# QQ-Plot mit ggplot2
res.plot <- ggplot(data.frame(res), aes(sample = res)) +
  stat_qq(color = "steelblue", size = 2) +
  stat_qq_line(color = "firebrick", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
     title = "QQ Plot of Transformed Residuals",
    x = "Theoretical Quantiles",
    y = "Observed Quantiles"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
res.plot

# Check heteroskedasticity (1.3.3.2)
plotHet <- ggplot(data.frame(fitted.values = women2$linpred, y=sqrt(abs(res))), aes(x=fitted.values, y=y)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth() 
plotHet 
## `geom_smooth()` using method = 'loess' and formula = 'y ~ x'

# Check association with excluded predictors
plotExcPred <- ggplot(data.frame(Weight=women2$Weight, Residuals=res), aes(x=Weight, y=Residuals)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth() 
plotExcPred
## `geom_smooth()` using method = 'loess' and formula = 'y ~ x'

ggplot(data=data.frame(residuals=res), aes(x=res)) + geom_histogram(bins=20)

## Model Info:

## 
## Fit Diagnostics:
##            mean   sd   10%   50%   90%
